title: On the semidefinite representability of continuous quadratic submodular minimization with applications to moment problems
contribution: Proves that the Shor SDP with only the RLT upper bounds is tight for box-constrained submodular QP when n <= 3 (any sign of c), certifies in exact arithmetic a counterexample at n = 4, and uses the result through moment duality for a new DRO ambiguity set and covariance bounds (read as arXiv v3, 2026).
problem_entry: Empty cell in a complexity table (submodular quadratic over [0,1]^n known polynomial only for DR-submodular or c <= 0), motivated by pricing with substitutes, a relaxed Chebyshev ambiguity set and covariance bounds (pp. 2-5).
key_idea: Use submodularity to drop the RLT lower bounds, prove the leaner SDP tight for n <= 3 via a completely positive certificate, break it at n = 4, and dualize the n <= 3 result into SDP approximations of a moment cone (pp. 9, 12, 14, 17-22).
assumptions: Box [0,1]^n, Q with nonpositive off-diagonals, c and diagonal unrestricted; DRO cost with -A_k(x) submodular and SDP-representable X; moment set with fixed means and diagonal second moments, off-diagonals bounded below, Sigma not required PSD (pp. 2, 15, 18, 21).
proof_devices: Pataki rank bound turned into r(r+1) <= 2(a+1) for extreme points with a active RLT upper bounds (Lemma 1, pp. 9-10)
Completely positive tightness certificate CP(J) subset of L (Lemma 2, p. 11)
Case analysis on rank and on counts of active s-lower/diagonal/s-upper inequalities after sorting by x (pp. 11-12)
Explicit rotation of a rank-2 factor into the cone J (Lemma 4, pp. 36-37)
Objective-nonincreasing line segment to more active inequalities or X >= xx^T (Lemma 5, pp. 37-39)
Inductive peeling Y = x1 ee^T + (1-x1) Y~ and rank-one subtraction (Lemma 6, pp. 40-41)
Index merging from identical columns under an active s-lower inequality, induction on n (Lemma 7, Proposition 5, pp. 41-42)
Moment-cone duality M0 = M1 + M2, M0* = K1 cap K2 (pp. 16-17)

Exact rational certificate: enumeration of 81 KKT active-set patterns plus a rational feasible point verified by Sylvester's criterion; rational point at denominator 10^8 surviving full RLT + triangle inequalities (Proposition 12, pp. 43-44)
Remark 1 maps the n = 4 proof failure (rank 3, l = 0, partial d,u) where the counterexample lies (pp. 13-14, 43)
experiments: 1,000 random submodular instances n in {4..20} plus 34,000 at n = 4..7 (Gurobi global QP vs Mosek SDP dual bound, gap threshold 1e-4: none exceeded, all but one rank-1 at n = 4..7); n = 3 pricing, DRO stratified sampling by enumerating 406 allocations, Laplacian-energy bounds vs Delage-Ye, and RLT/triangle gap test on the counterexample (pp. 26-36, 44).
positioning: Extends Kim & Kojima 2003 (c <= 0) and Anstreicher & Burer 2010 (n = 2); offers an alternative to the Delage-Ye moment set and reports that neither subsumes the other; credits Hossjer & Sjolander for the n = 2 covariance bound (pp. 5, 7-8, 25, 34).
writing: Claims at their proved level (provably tight n <= 3, empirically tight beyond), theorem assembled from propositions proved in section 6, two projection figures for geometry, and the earlier error credited by name (pp. 1, 12-13, 44-46).
limits_future: Complexity for n >= 4 open (needs a different certificate or a hardness reduction); triangle cuts close >99.9% but not all of the gap; future: infimal-convolution combination of ambiguity sets and redundancy of RLT bounds for sparse Q (pp. 34, 44, 46).

method_links.note: Small-dimension proof (n <= 3), boundary published at the first certified counterexample (n = 4), and the kitchen sink (full RLT + triangle inequalities) shown not to close the gap.
Dual-bound gap with 1e-4 threshold over 35,000 random instances, exact rational counterexample certificate, genericity read into the verdict, error credited to Shaoning Han.
Tightness judged by the SDP dual objective against a known global QP optimum, without an eigenvalue-ratio second signal.
Tightness proved through the completely positive representation of box QP (CP(J)).
Random panel deliberately placed outside the known polynomial cases but not filtered to baseline failures; the paper notes it does not reach the non-generic gap configuration.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: prove tightness of the leanest relaxation the objective's sign structure allows
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Only RLT upper bounds kept because submodularity makes the lower bounds unlikely to bind; tightness of the lean relaxation is the stronger statement.
Remark 1 names the rank-3 partial-activity configuration the proof cannot handle at n = 4; Example 4 lies exactly there.

transferable: Pataki-style counting r(r+1) <= 2(a+1) to bound the rank of extreme optimal solutions, then handle each rank separately (pp. 9-12).
Prove SDP tightness by moving an optimal solution, without objective loss, to one with a completely positive factorization (pp. 11, 36-41).
Index merging under an active coupling constraint to induct on n while preserving the problem class (pp. 41-42).
Certify a tiny nonconvex QP optimum by enumerating all 3^n KKT active-set patterns over the rationals, and a relaxation value by a rational feasible point (p. 43).
Judge tightness with the SDP dual objective (a valid bound) against the global optimum, and read a gap-free random panel as rarity evidence, not a theorem (p. 27).
Open with a domain-by-function-class complexity table and fill the empty cell, with a footnote fixing the scope (p. 3).
Project onto (objective, slack of a violated cut) to show the gap and a cut's effect in one figure (pp. 44-45).
coauthors: Karthik Natarajan, Rick Willemsen (SUTD); Willemsen appears on the v3 read here

quotes.text: The experiment is therefore best understood as evidence that violations of tightness are rare.
What fails at n ≥ 4 is therefore this particular semidefinite certificate, not necessarily tractability itself.

title: Optimization over trained neural networks: Going large with gradient-based algorithms
contribution: Proposes Gradient Walk local search over trained ReLU networks (PPGA with perturbation restarts, PPGALR with a linear-region step valve) whose cheaper iterations beat prior LP-based local search as networks grow (read as arXiv v2).
problem_entry: Exact MILP models of ReLU networks are weak or huge; local search over linear regions scales better, and LP Walk beat MILP Walk by cheaper iterations, so push to an even cheaper iteration (pp. 1-4).
key_idea: Projected gradient ascent with the closed-form region-constant gradient, restarts triggered by a window of small improvements, and a ratio-test 'valve' that rescales steps to cross enough linear regions (pp. 6-9).
assumptions: Polytope (box) domain; feed-forward ReLU network with weights and biases in [-1,1]; untrained networks at random initialization as test functions (pp. 5-6, 8, 10).
proof_devices: n/a for theorems; per-step complexity count O(dm^2 + n0 m) vs one LP per SimplexWalk step (section 4.3, p. 11)
experiments: 36 network configurations x 20 evaluation seeds, 7,200 s runs; gradient methods tuned by grid search on 5 disjoint seeds with voting; baselines PGA and SimplexWalk; Dolan-More profiles at 30/60/120 min and split by size; losses reported; single-instance step-size case study (pp. 9-15).
positioning: Continues the MILP Walk -> LP Walk trend of cheaper specialized local search; MILP strengthening literature as context; smooth saddle-escape perturbation work set apart because saddles lie on nondifferentiable boundaries (pp. 1-4, 7-8, 15).
writing: Conference style with toy 2-input network figures tracing each walk; two-fold contribution statement; hedged explanations of results (pp. 1-4, 12-14).
limits_future: No convergence theory, no safeguard for too-large steps, weights in [-1,1], untrained networks only; future: robustness to large learning rates, other landscape features, other CL models, specific function families (pp. 8, 10, 15-16).

method_links.note: Algorithm first, no convergence theory, value shown by benchmarking against the strongest prior local method.
Methods are grid-search tuned rather than run at defaults; valve parameters made adaptive for fairness to methods with fewer hyperparameters.

transferable: Replace a gradient-norm stopping test by a progress-window test on objective improvement in piecewise-linear landscapes (pp. 7-8).
Ratio test over neuron pre-activations along the gradient to estimate distance to the next linear region and rescale the step (pp. 8-9).
Tune hyperparameters on seeds disjoint from evaluation seeds and choose by vote across tuning instances (pp. 10-11).
Split performance profiles by each size parameter to find what drives a win, report where the baseline still wins, and show profiles at several time budgets (pp. 11-14).
coauthors: Jiatai Tong (Northwestern), Yilin Zhu, Thiago Serra (Iowa); Burer last author

quotes.text: Hence, the size of ∇f(x) is not a reliable measure of local optimality in our case.
In a nutshell, we double down on the trend of using specialized local search with lower per-iteration cost to find better solutions in constraint learning.

title: An extended validity domain for constraint learning
contribution: Introduces CH+, a validity domain for constraint learning that takes the convex hull of data in the extended space (x, predictions, objective), justified by an exact convex-hull reformulation, and shows on 37,800 experiments, two stylized models and an avocado case that it mainly cuts function-value and feasibility error (read as arXiv v2, 2025).
problem_entry: Embedded ML models extrapolate badly away from training data, and all existing validity domains (Box, CH, enlarged CH, SVM, isolation forest) act only in x-space (pp. 2-3, 6-7).
key_idea: The true problem is linear minimization over the convex hull of the graph (x, y, f(x)) of feasible points (Proposition 1), so constrain (x, y-hat, f(x)) to the hull of the extended data, whose projection lies inside CH (pp. 7-9).
assumptions: Theory assumes noiseless h evaluations; practice uses noisy data; regression only; Proposition 2 needs the sample hulls to fill conv(F+) in the limit (pp. 3-4, 7-8).
proof_devices: Convex-combination argument giving v* = min phi over conv(F+) (Proposition 1, p. 8)
Sandwich/limit argument for sample hulls (Proposition 2, p. 8)
Projection inclusion proj_x(CH+) subset of CH giving v-hat(CH+) >= v-hat(CH) (Proposition 3, p. 9)
1-D worked example with four samples showing the error trade-off (Figure 1, pp. 10-11)
experiments: Protocol from Shi et al. 2024: 37,800 experiments (7 functions x 2 samplers x 3 N x 3 noise x 100 seeds x 3 models), medians scaled to Box = 1.00 with means in the supplement; enlarged hulls; n1 = 20 test with prohibitive combinations disclosed; norm-ball and pricing stylized models; avocado case study without ground truth; sensitivity analyses (pp. 10-24, 28-35).
positioning: Within CL taxonomies (Kotary et al., Sadana et al., Fajemisin et al.); neutral review of existing validity domains; compares against the strongest recent one (isolation forest, Shi et al.) and reports being faster (pp. 1-3, 6-7).
writing: Intuition, then short propositions, then hedged claims ('we believe'); worse optimal-value errors argued for via the feasibility argument; variant naming flagged each time; minor inconsistencies remain in v2 (pp. 9-10, 20-21, 24, 35).
limits_future: Not best on optimal-value error, no guidelines for choosing a validity domain, somewhat noise sensitive, epsilon can be too loose, needs data on all variables; future: feasibility, other domains in the extended space, model-aware domains, classification (pp. 20, 23-25, 33).

method_links.note: Same lift-to-one-convex-hull reflex (Proposition 1), but the hull is inner-approximated from data and used as a constraint rather than relaxed by a cone.
Ground-truth testbed with disclosed exclusions of prohibitive runs, but the testbed is the competitor's benchmark, not one engineered where the incumbent fails.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: carry the lift-and-hull reformulation from conic relaxation into ML-embedded optimization
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Exact reformulation over the hull of the graph in (x, y, phi), then a data hull as validity domain; the same group continues the CL line in S056.

transferable: Ask for the exact convex reformulation of the true problem in a lifted space before designing a heuristic constraint, then use its data-driven inner approximation (pp. 7-9).
Extended-space convex hull of (x, y-hat, f(x)) samples as a validity domain (pp. 9-10).
Build 'sandwich' variants between the old and new method for partial data (p. 9).
Adopt the main competitor's published protocol for the comparison (p. 10).
Report medians normalized to the simplest baseline and give means in a supplement with a statement on whether conclusions change (pp. 13, 28-29).
Judge a ground-truth-free case study against an empirical benchmark (average revenue) (pp. 22, 24).

quotes.text: We believe that overall this constitutes an advantage of CH+ and its variants because, generally speaking, one cannot have true optimality without true feasibility.
At this time, we unfortunately lack a solid set of practical guidelines for choosing the best validity domain in common situations.
